patterns.usage_note: たがる is たい plus the suffix がる, which recasts an inner feeling as behavior an observer can see, so it reports a third party's desire as displayed rather than felt. It attaches to the masu-stem and conjugates as a godan verb; non-past たがる usually reads as habitual or repeated, while たがっている describes a wish someone is showing right now. Unlike たい, たがる marks its object only with を; the が option disappears when you switch. Because it frames the person from the outside it can sound detached or faintly critical, so speakers usually avoid it about a superior, and a bare first-person subject is likewise avoided except when describing one's own habitual character (私は昔から知りたがる性格だ).

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]はいつも私[わたし]のゲームを借[か]りたがる。
examples.english: My little brother is always after my games.

examples.ruby: 同僚[どうりょう]はさっきから早[はや]く帰[かえ]りたがっている。
examples.english: My coworker has been itching to head home for a while now.

examples.ruby: 父[ちち]は誰[だれ]にでも昔話[むかしばなし]をしたがります。
examples.english: My father is only too eager to tell his old stories to anyone at all.
